dated.quote: In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim king of Judah came Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon unto Jerusalem, and besieged it.
dated.note: Dates the opening events, not the whole book. 1:21 adds that Daniel “continued even unto the first year of king Cyrus”.

dated.quote: And in the second year of the reign of Nebuchadnezzar Nebuchadnezzar dreamed dreams, wherewith his spirit was troubled, and his sleep brake from him.
In that night was Belshazzar the king of the Chaldeans slain. And Darius the Median took the kingdom, being about threescore and two years old.

It pleased Darius to set over the kingdom an hundred and twenty princes, which should be over the whole kingdom;
dated.note: 6:28 adds that Daniel prospered “in the reign of Darius, and in the reign of Cyrus the Persian”.

dated.quote: In the first year of Belshazzar king of Babylon Daniel had a dream and visions of his head upon his bed: then he wrote the dream, and told the sum of the matters.
In the third year of the reign of king Belshazzar a vision appeared unto me, even unto me Daniel, after that which appeared unto me at the first.

In the first year of Darius the son of Ahasuerus, of the seed of the Medes, which was made king over the realm of the Chaldeans; In the first year of his reign I Daniel understood by books the number of the years, whereof the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah the prophet, that he would accomplish seventy years in the desolations of Jerusalem.
dated.note: “Ahasuerus” here is named as Darius’s father; the site keeps him as a separate person (ahasuerus-dan-9-1), not the king of Esther.

dated.quote: In the third year of Cyrus king of Persia a thing was revealed unto Daniel, whose name was called Belteshazzar; and the thing was true, but the time appointed was long: and he understood the thing, and had understanding of the vision.
dated.why: The revelation begun at 10:1 continues as one speech of the messenger through 11 to the end of the book (12:13).

dated.quote: Also I in the first year of Darius the Mede, even I, stood to confirm and to strengthen him.
dated.note: The messenger recalls what he did “in the first year of Darius the Mede”; the vision itself is dated by 10:1 (the third year of Cyrus).
